patterns.title: Word-by-word Montgomery addition preserves validity and modular sum
patterns.exact_property: addmod_correct proves both modular addition after Montgomery decoding and valid (addmod a b) for valid inputs.

root.statement: (forall a (_ : valid a) b (_ : valid b), eval (from_montgomerymod (addmod a b)) mod m = (eval (from_montgomerymod a) + eval (from_montgomerymod b)) mod m) /\ (forall a (_ : valid a) b (_ : valid b), valid (addmod a b)).

hypotheses: valid a and valid b, where valid x := small x /\ 0 <= eval x < m.
proof_slice_trace: WordByWordMontgomery.addmod is defined as @add bitwidth n m_enc a b.
The root theorem addmod_correct splits into the decoded modular-sum equality and output validity.
The proof invokes the representation-level eval_add property for value preservation and small_add/add_bound plus the small N modulus encoding facts for the range side.
The shared representation invariant is valid x := small x /\ 0 <= eval x < m; eval is the positional evaluator at uweight bitwidth.
The theorem is in Section modops, whose arithmetic parameters include the Montgomery inverse conditions and modulus/width bounds.

patterns.title: Carried limb multiplication preserves the modular product
patterns.exact_property: eval_carry_mulmod states that the derived carry_mulmod program evaluates to the product of its inputs modulo s - Associational.eval c for length-n inputs.

root.statement: forall (f g : list Z) (Hf : length f = n) (Hg : length g = n), (eval weight n (carry_mulmod f g)) mod (s - Associational.eval c) = (eval weight n f * eval weight n g) mod (s - Associational.eval c).

hypotheses: length c = len_c; length idxs = len_idxs.
length f = n; length g = n.
proof_slice_trace: ModOps defines weight i as 2^(-(-(limbwidth_num * i) / limbwidth_den)) and proves weight properties under limbwidth_good.
The root obligation is attached with Derive carry_mulmod SuchThat ... As eval_carry_mulmod.

Its proof rewrites through eval_mulmod for the abstract modular operation and eval_chained_carries for the configured idxs carry schedule, then relates the derived program definition to that schedule.
Arithmetic.Core supplies the positional and associational evaluators and carry lemmas used by the proof.
patterns.reuse_use_case: Use this obligation pattern when deriving a fixed-width limb program from a modular arithmetic operation: preserve the weighted positional result modulo the declared modulus and account for each configured carry stage.
